rationale: This is a cosmetic operator swap on the archive's "Intangible Operating Leverage" (oancf/sale in place of oiadp/sale), with the cash-margin element already probed by "Intangible Cash Realization," so it offers no substantively new mechanism.

It is a third numerator variant of the already-tested (at+gdwl)-denominated profitability family, and subtracting xint injects a leverage tilt that confounds the stated "validated acquisition" story with the well-known leverage/distress effect rather than isolating it.

The NEG combined with a negative expected sign double-negates, making this economically identical to the archive's gen-1 winner "Intangible Operating Leverage" with gdwl substituted for intan — a relabeling, not a new hypothesis.

The bounded margin-level-to-volatility quality term is a genuinely different construction from the level and first-difference interactions already tested and is internally consistent in sign, though the signal risks being dominated by the intan/at intensity leg and overlaps known profitability-persistence/earnings-volatility results.

Adding non-goodwill intangibles (already inside at) to the denominator is a minor perturbation of plain operating profitability, so the signal will be nearly collinear with the standard profitability anomaly and with the archive's (at+gdwl)-scaled returns.

The expression is internally inconsistent with its rationale — "reversing the incremental research expense" requires the level xrd/sale, not its first difference — and it sums unit-mismatched sales-scaled and asset-scaled terms with arbitrary equal weights on a low-coverage R&D subsample.
